title: Secretary of State of Arizona

context.text: Fontes won the 2022 election; Kolodin won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 58.3% over Gina Swoboda, and Duwayne Collier won the Green primary.

candidates.name: Adrian Fontes
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Supporting Arizona's established voting methods, including early voting, vote-by-mail and in-person voting.
Protecting voter privacy; his survey says a judge ruled in his favor when the federal government sought private voter information.
Seeking more state and federal funding to modernize and secure election systems.

record.text: A federal judge dismissed with prejudice, on April 28, 2026, the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking Arizona's unredacted voter rolls; the dismissal granted Fontes's motion to dismiss. He had refused to sign two memoranda of understanding with the department.

candidates.name: Alexander Kolodin

priorities.text: Restoring trust in elections through transparency and accountability; Ballotpedia quotes his campaign website as saying he will bring both to the office "so every Arizonan knows their vote counts."

record.text: Sponsored a bill to increase voter ID requirements in Arizona that voters will decide on the November ballot, according to KJZZ.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign website was not loaded; his positions on proof of citizenship were not found as his own direct statements. KJZZ notes he played a part in lawsuits challenging 2020 and 2022 election results.

candidates.name: Duwayne Collier
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or biography found.

researchNotes: Slate from Ballotpedia's list of general-election candidates and FOX 10 Phoenix's voter guide (Collier, Fontes, Kolodin). The Arizona Secretary of State's candidate pages returned 403 to automated requests, so the official certified list was not checked. Kolodin's priority is quoted as Ballotpedia reproduces his campaign website; the site itself could not be read.
